title: Shunten Dynasty
capsule: The Shunten dynasty was the second ruling line of Okinawa Island, founded c. 1187 when Shunten—traditionally described as the son of the Japanese warrior Minamoto no Tametomo—overthrew the usurper Riyū and established paramountcy over the island's regional lords (aji) during the Gusuku period. The dynasty comprised three rulers and is better characterized as a paramount chieftaincy than a centralized monarchy; its foundation legends reflect growing Japanese cultural influence in the Ryukyus. It ended when the third ruler Gihon abdicated c. 1259 in favor of his regent Eiso, who founded the succeeding Eiso dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty is known primarily from the 15th-century Chūzan Seikan chronicle; its territorial extent and precise chronology rest on later tradition rather than contemporary documentation.
